title: Divide with remainders and say what the remainder means

lesson.title: What Is Left Over? Division With Remainders

steps.say: You already know how to divide big numbers into equal groups. But here is the thing — real life does not always split evenly! Today we look at what happens to the little bit that is left over, and what that leftover is trying to tell us.

Imagine you have fourteen granola bars, and you want to put four bars in each snack bag. Watch what happens. One bag, two bags, three bags — and then you have two bars sitting there, all alone. Two bars is not enough to fill a fourth bag. So we say fourteen divided by four is three, remainder two. The remainder is just the part that could not make another full group.

visual.caption: 14 granola bars: 3 full bags of 4, with 2 bars left over

steps.say: Here is a secret rule about the leftover. The remainder always has to be smaller than the number in each group. If you had eight bars left over when your bags hold four, you could still fill another bag! So when someone says twenty divided by six is two, remainder eight, we know right away that is wrong — eight is bigger than six. The right answer is three groups of six, which is eighteen, and two left over.

visual.caption: 20 split into groups of 6: three full groups, 2 left over — the leftover must be less than 6

steps.say: Now the most important part — the remainder is never just garbage. It depends on the story! Say twenty kids are going to the aquarium, and each van holds six kids. Twenty divided by six is three, remainder two. Some kids answer three vans. But wait — those two kids would be standing in the parking lot! They still need a ride, so we need a fourth van. Same numbers, but the story tells us to round up to four vans.

visual.caption: The 2 leftover kids still need a van — so 4 vans in all

steps.say: So always finish by asking yourself: what does my leftover mean here? Two bars left over means two bars for later. Two kids left over means one more van. Same remainder, different meaning — you get to decide by thinking about the story.

lesson.answer: The remainder is the part that could not fill another group — always smaller than the group size, and the story tells you what to do with it.

practice.question: You baked twenty-three muffins for the school bake sale in Kelowna, and each box holds five muffins. Draw groups of five dots if it helps! How many boxes can you fill completely, how many muffins are left over, and how many boxes do you need if you want to bring every single muffin?
practice.answer: Twenty-three divided by five is four, remainder three. You can fill four boxes completely, with three muffins left over. To bring every muffin you need five boxes — the last box just is not full.
